reader.requirement: At 1985, after a successful WRITE of an indexed file named in a SAME RECORD AREA clause, the released logical record must remain available in record-name-1's area and as a record of every other file of that clause (any organization, any record shape: fixed, variable-length, elementary); without the clause its availability is undefined (not observable). The witness l1c37 covers only two sequential files.

edition-consulted.switches: Constructs.FromLiteral2002: FROM literal-1 (figurative included) refused below 2002 (COBOL0871)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior over KeyedIoEmitter.cs EmitWrite, SequentialIoEmitter.cs Begin/End/EmitReleasedRecordAlsoAvailable, FileControlBinder.IoControl.cs LinkSameRecordArea and FileModel.SameRecordAreaPeers: none; the SAME RECORD AREA overlay (implicit redefinition) and the out-of-line store are edition-free. The only edition gate on WRITE ... FROM is the 2002 literal operand.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the also-available mechanism is one arm; only FROM literal-1 is an edition arm (refused at 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c37 covers sequential files only; not exercised: an indexed record-name-1 (this module's rule), variable-length and elementary (out-of-line) peer records, a failed WRITE

reader.notes: SAME RECORD AREA files' character-window records are linked as implicit redefinitions of one anchor (LinkSameRecordArea), so a released record is in every peer's area for free; an out-of-line (variable-length or slot-carried elementary) record on either side gets an emitted store after the WRITE (Begin/EndReleasedRecord, used by KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite). Probes at --std 85 with indexed random, dynamic and sequential files, ODO and an elementary numeric peer all showed the record available.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-011/c2/r1.cob (--std 85): indexed RANDOM F1 (two 01s) in SAME RECORD AREA with a relative F2, a sequential RECORD VARYING/ODO F4 (also in a SAME AREA with F2) and a SORT file SD SF, only F1 ever opened: after WRITE R1 'K0105ABCDE' -> 00, R2 'K0105' N 105, R4 positions 3-4 '10', RS 'K0105A|BCDE'; WRITE R1B (second 01, 4 chars) -> 00 and R1/R2/RS show 'XYZW'; reread both records 00. Peers never opened, a sort-merge peer and a SAME AREA subset all see the released record. OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR2 the text is in GR2.
